evals.prompt: Design the connection manager screen for our macOS database client. Make it look premium and Apple-quality.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to style before structuring: writes the experience brief first, produces a native component map classifying every region as NATIVE, NATIVE-COMPOSED, or CUSTOM, then generates structurally different alternatives with realistic fixtures, and requires a human selection before any implementation.

evals.prompt: Review this screenshot of our records workspace against our design standards.
evals.expected_output: Scores the eight rubric categories against the rendered evidence, checks the hard-failure list explicitly, orders findings by severity from broken workflow down to micro-polish, names what can be deleted, and flags any required state that has no screenshot as a finding, and the review includes a Preserve section and the score-caps table.

evals.prompt: We selected alternative B. Proceed without recording why it won or what was rejected.
evals.expected_output: Stops at the Stage-4 selection gate until one direction is selected and records why it won, what was rejected, and which risks remain before implementation.

evals.prompt: Build a custom sidebar component because the native one looks plain.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the custom classification for lacking a user-need reason, requires the native alternatives evaluated and why each was insufficient, notes that a custom control weaker than an available native component is a hard failure, and demands the full custom component contract including keyboard focus, inactive-window state, accessibility, and a menu-bar command equivalent before any implementation.

evals.prompt: Use systematize mode on this approved screen and its review to turn accepted decisions into reusable system knowledge.
evals.expected_output: Executes the defined systematize procedure: lands reusable component-map entries, rubric rules, and anti-patterns in their owning design references; lands token roles as committed values consumed by tailrocks-macos-prototype and tailrocks-swift-best-practices without emitting code; and completes only when every output is landed in its owning file.

evals.prompt: Give the final design verdict for this review, including what survives correction.
evals.expected_output: Produces a Preserve list, applies every hard failure and score cap, orders corrections, and completes only when the rubric threshold is met, no hard failure remains, and required rendered states have evidence.
